summary: End-to-end ML platforms unify training, fine-tuning, experiment tracking, model registry, deployment, and governance across the ML lifecycle, and in 2026 the market (valued at ~$4.39B and growing at ~45.8% CAGR) is dominated by the three hyperscaler offerings alongside Databricks. You need a full platform when you train or fine-tune custom models, require reproducibility, lineage, governance, and scalable serving infrastructure; if you only consume frontier models via inference, a hosted model API is cheaper and simpler, but once you need custom training, monitoring, cost control, and compliance at scale, a dedicated MLOps platform becomes essential.

platforms.name: Microsoft Azure Machine Learning
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go based on compute (VM/GPU hours), storage, and managed endpoints; no platform license fee. Enterprise agreements available.
platforms.best_for: Enterprises already in the Microsoft ecosystem needing strong governance and lifecycle management (top GigaOm enterprise-readiness score 2.95/3).

platforms.name: Amazon SageMaker AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per-second billing for compute (training/inference instances), plus storage and endpoint hosting; no upfront license.
platforms.best_for: AWS-native teams needing robust production deployment, modular tooling, and deep ecosystem integration (GigaOm 2.83/3, leads in production deployment).

platforms.name: Databricks (MLflow + Mosaic AI)
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based (DBUs) on top of underlying cloud compute; tiered by workload type. No fixed license.
platforms.best_for: Data-centric organizations wanting unified data, analytics, ML, and AI on a lakehouse architecture, multi-cloud flexibility.

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI (Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform)
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go for compute, training, prediction, and pipeline usage; managed GenAI services priced per token/usage.
platforms.best_for: GCP-native teams wanting tightly integrated feature store, opinionated pipelines, and managed GenAI/agent workflows (GigaOm 2.12/3, gaps in governance).

platforms.name: DataRobot
platforms.pricing: Enterprise subscription/license (quote-based); tiered by users and deployment scale.
platforms.best_for: Enterprises wanting automated ML and managed infrastructure without heavy MLOps engineering overhead.

platforms.name: Dataiku
platforms.best_for: Cross-functional teams (analysts + data scientists) wanting a collaborative, visual end-to-end platform with governance.

platforms.name: Weights & Biases (CoreWeave)
platforms.pricing: Freemium for individuals; team/enterprise subscription per user with usage-based tiers.
platforms.best_for: ML research and engineering teams needing best-in-class experiment tracking, reproducibility, and LLM evaluation layered on any training stack.

platforms.name: H2O.ai
platforms.pricing: Open-source core (free); enterprise subscription for Driverless AI and managed cloud (quote-based).
platforms.best_for: Teams wanting open-source-rooted AutoML plus enterprise GenAI tooling and strong explainability.

platforms.name: Domino Data Lab
platforms.pricing: Enterprise subscription/license (quote-based), consumption tiers for compute.
platforms.best_for: Regulated enterprises (finance, pharma, life sciences) needing reproducibility, governance, and hybrid/on-prem compute control.

platforms.name: MLflow
platforms.pricing: Free and open-source; cost is self-hosting infrastructure or bundled via Databricks.
platforms.best_for: Teams with DevOps skills wanting an open-source, framework-agnostic backbone for tracking, registry, and deployment.

platforms.name: Kubeflow
platforms.pricing: Free and open-source; cost is Kubernetes infrastructure and engineering overhead.
platforms.best_for: Kubernetes-native teams with strong DevOps capability wanting portable, scalable ML pipelines without vendor lock-in.

platforms.name: Modal
platforms.pricing: Usage-based per-second billing for CPU/GPU compute; no fixed platform fee, free starter credits.
platforms.best_for: Developers and teams wanting serverless, code-first GPU compute for training and deploying models and AI apps without managing infrastructure.
